decoys.summary: The primitive-root fast paths return after parsing the first token without checking for a second root, so to_owned_value accepts documents such as `true false` or `17 {}` and silently discards the trailing JSON value.
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify acceptance of a whitespace-separated second top-level JSON value after a primitive root through the normal DOM parsing API, attributing it to the primitive-root success path. Merely discussing unusual number delimiters is insufficient.

refutation.evidence: decoy_1_trailing_root_is_rejected passed: 45 documents combining 9 root kinds and 5 second-root suffixes were rejected; all 9 valid roots followed only by JSON whitespace were accepted. In build_tape each primitive success path requires i == structural_indexes.len(); otherwise it returns TrailingData (true: lines 350-354, false: 362-366, null: 374-378, string: 381-385, negative number: 388-393, nonnegative number: 396-401). Stage 1 records the next whitespace-delimited token as a pseudo-structural at lib.rs:279, so the next root prevents that equality. This does not concern the separately listed real NUL-after-number defect. The corresponding named test and its result are preserved in evidence/negative_controls.rs and evidence/probe.log.

decoys.summary: Ignoring an unknown struct field whose value is a nested array or object consumes only its container header: deserialize_ignored_any forwards to deserialize_any without advancing over the descendants, so a following recognized field is misread or reported missing.
decoys.match_rule: The report must allege that ordinary derived struct deserialization fails to skip the descendants of an unknown nested field, for example the ignored field in {"ignored":[{"a":[1]}],"keep":42}. The alleged trigger must be standard unknown-field ignoring, rather than a fixed-length tuple/array target or a custom visitor that stops early.

refutation.evidence: decoy_2_ignored_nested_field_is_drained passed for six unknown container values, from empty arrays/objects to alternating nested arrays and objects; every following keep field was read as 42. The forwarding at serde/de.rs:349 dispatches IgnoredAny to deserialize_any, which passes an array or object access visitor at lines 33-34. Serde 1.0.219 IgnoredAny::visit_seq loops next_element until None and visit_map loops next_entry until None, recursively deserializing IgnoredAny descendants. simd-json CommaSeparated decrements the remaining length and delegates each element/key/value seed (lines 433-437, 456-470). Thus this visitor drains the entire subtree, unlike the distinct known issue with visitors for fixed-length targets that stop early. The locked dependency implementation is included as numbered excerpts in evidence/source-guards.txt. The corresponding named test and its result are preserved in evidence/negative_controls.rs and evidence/probe.log.

false_findings.title: Serde small-integer deserialization wraps out-of-range values
false_findings.body: The small-integer readers narrow a 64-bit StaticNode before delivering it to the Serde visitor, without validating that the original integer fits the requested type. Deserializing JSON `256` into u8 therefore succeeds with 0, and deserializing `128` into i8 succeeds with -128. Applications using these bounded types to validate numeric input receive wrapped values instead of a deserialization error, even on a fresh deserializer containing one valid JSON number.

refutation.evidence: false_1_small_integer_ranges_are_checked passed: u8 accepted 0 and 255 but rejected 256, 511, -1, and u64::MAX; i8 accepted -128 and 127 but rejected -129, 128, 255, and i64::MAX. parse_u8 and parse_i8 call StaticNode.as_u8/as_i8 and turn None into ExpectedUnsigned/ExpectedSigned (serde.rs:222-225 and 278-281). The locked value-trait 0.11.0 ValueAsScalar implementations use as_u64/as_i64 followed by try_into().ok(), not a wrapping cast (base.rs:59-60 and 97-98). This check is distinct from the known exhausted-deserializer unchecked-next issue: every test uses fresh nonempty input. Dependency guards are preserved in evidence/source-guards.txt. The corresponding named test and its result are preserved in evidence/negative_controls.rs and evidence/probe.log.

false_findings.title: Compact DOM serialization emits unescaped object keys
false_findings.body: The compact object writer surrounds keys with quote bytes and sends the decoded key to write_simple_str_content, bypassing the escaping used for string values. An object with a quote, backslash, or newline in its key is consequently encoded with those bytes verbatim. For example, a parsed object whose key is `quote"key` cannot be encoded back into valid JSON with encode(); the same fast object-writing pattern is used for borrowed values.

refutation.evidence: false_2_dom_object_keys_are_escaped passed: quote, backslash, newline, NUL, tab, and Unicode keys survived all 24 round trips across owned/borrowed and compact/pretty encodings, verified by serde_json parsing and exact object equality. The compact writers call write_simple_str_content at owned/serialize.rs:151,157 and borrowed/serialize.rs:149,155. In locked value-trait 0.11.0 this helper calls write_string_rust, which scans the ESCAPED table and invokes write_string_container for any escapable byte; that function writes backslash escapes or unicode escapes. "Simple" skips SIMD setup, not JSON escaping. The complete helper/table excerpts are in evidence/source-guards.txt. The corresponding named test and its result are preserved in evidence/negative_controls.rs and evidence/probe.log.

false_findings.title: Reusing Buffers carries structural indexes into the next document
false_findings.body: fill_tape reuses buffer.structural_indexes and sends it back through the structural scanner without resetting the old entries. After parsing a long object or array, parsing a shorter document with the same Buffers therefore leaves indexes from the first document visible to stage 2. A normal sequence such as a long array followed by `{}` through to_owned_value_with_buffers can fail with a syntax/trailing-data error despite the second document being valid; a previous parse error can also poison subsequent calls.

refutation.evidence: false_3_reused_buffers_reset_structural_state passed 33 sequential parses using one Buffers initially sized zero, cycling from a 100-object array to shorter objects, arrays, numbers, and strings, including recovery from malformed/truncated/whitespace-only inputs. All success/error decisions and decoded values matched fresh serde_json results. _find_structural_bits unconditionally calls structural_indexes.clear() at lib.rs:890 before reserving and scanning; quote/backslash/error state is initialized locally for each call (901,903,921). fill_tape overwrites the current input and its full SIMD padding (819-831), while build_tape clears the output vector and stack (stage2.rs:107,111). Capacity reuse does not preserve logical indexes. The corresponding named test and its result are preserved in evidence/negative_controls.rs and evidence/probe.log.

false_findings.title: NEON string fast path accepts raw control characters inside quoted strings
false_findings.body: The aarch64 NEON string fast path searches only for backslashes and quotes, then directly returns the string when a quote appears first. Since it never checks bytes below 0x20, a quoted string containing a literal newline or tab and no backslash is accepted by to_owned_value. The missing check also lets control bytes inside long strings cross SIMD block boundaries and reach the DOM, accepting text that JSON requires to be rejected.

refutation.evidence: false_4_raw_control_bytes_in_strings_are_rejected passed on aarch64: all 32 raw control bytes at 12 positions spanning 16-, 32-, and 64-byte boundaries were rejected (384 cases), while all 384 escaped unicode equivalents parsed and contained the expected byte. The string decoder runs only after stage 1: fill_tape invokes find_structural_bits and propagates its error at lib.rs:833-834 before calling build_tape at 837. Stage1Parse::find_quote_mask_and_bits computes unsigned input <= 0x1f and ORs its intersection with the quote mask into error_mask (195-196); both full and tail chunks invoke it (940,986), and a nonzero error_mask returns Syntax at 1023-1024. The NEON unsigned comparison implementing this guard is neon/stage1.rs:98-105. This claim concerns controls inside strings, not the known NUL-after-number delimiter defect. The corresponding named test and its result are preserved in evidence/negative_controls.rs and evidence/probe.log.

false_findings.title: into_static widens borrowed DOM lifetimes without owning nested strings
false_findings.body: BorrowedValue::into_static uses transmute to widen the lifetime of string Cows, while its container cases rebuild arrays and objects without detaching all nested strings and object keys from the input slice. Calling to_borrowed_value on an object containing nested arrays/objects and then into_static can thus return a BorrowedValue<'static> that still points into the original mutable input. Overwriting or dropping that input changes the converted value or leaves dangling string references, despite the safe public API advertising a static result.

refutation.evidence: false_5_into_static_owns_nested_strings_and_keys passed: the input DOM initially contained a borrowed string; after into_static a recursive inspection verified that all eight string values/object keys in a nested fixture were Cow::Owned. Only after that ownership assertion, the probe overwrote and dropped the input, then confirmed exact JSON equality. There is also a structural proof: the string branch first executes s.into_owned() and Cow::from(String), and only then transmutes the owning value (borrowed.rs:113-116); arrays recursively call Value::into_static (119); objects own each key with k.into_owned() and recursively convert every value (121-124); static scalars contain no borrow (127). These exhaustive enum arms ensure the lifetime widening never retains an input-backed string. The corresponding named test and its result are preserved in evidence/negative_controls.rs and evidence/probe.log.
